title: Cards and optics: the parts inside a switch
summary: Find the card the closets hang off, the optic one link needs, and what a swap takes down.

sources.claim: Optics (transceivers) are hot-removable and hot-insertable field-replaceable units: they come out and go in without powering the device off.
sources.cite: Juniper Networks, Maintain Transceivers, EX4400 Switch Hardware Guide (the page shows no date)

sources.claim: A modular device reports each card in its slot and each optic under the card it sits in, each with its own part number and serial.
sources.cite: Juniper Networks, show chassis hardware, Junos CLI reference, MX960 sample output

steps.title: Parts you can pull
steps.body: Bigger switches take cards: a card slides into a slot and brings its own ports. A fibre port is only a cage until an optic, a small transceiver, is pushed into it. Cards and optics are field-replaceable, each with its own part number and serial, so they are tracked like devices. In Fathom a card's ports stay on the device and say which card they are on; the optic is part of its port.

steps.title: The card
steps.prompt: Both closets and the server reach the rest through one card. Click the device it sits in.
steps.hint: Follow the aqua cables back from sw-a and sw-b.
steps.after: core-1, slot 1: a four-port SFP+ card. Its ports are 1/1 to 1/4. Open core-1's Ports tab to see the card and which cages hold an optic.

steps.title: One optic, one link
steps.prompt: The optic in core-1 port 1/2 is failing. Click the cable that goes dark while it is swapped.
steps.hint: Port 1/2 is on the card in slot 1. Which closet does it feed?
steps.after: Closet B's uplink. Optics come out and go in with the switch powered, but while the cage is empty nothing reaches sw-b or desktop-2.

steps.title: Through the card
steps.after: Both hops on core-1, in on 1/2 and out on 1/3, are ports on the same card. Take the card out and every closet loses the server at once; swap one optic and only its link goes.

steps.title: Keeping track
steps.body: Inventory's Parts list holds every card, power supply and optic with where it sits and its serial. Paste show inventory or show chassis hardware onto a device and Fathom offers what it reports. When a part fails, a maintenance plan's Swap a part step says which ports go down and records the new serial when you mark it done.
